clue.text: I don't care where TV actor originally worked

indicators.note: worked in the sense of worked over or kneaded, so the letters are reshaped
originally points to the opening letter of the word actor

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off the question of where a television actor once had a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' shuffles WHERE, TV and A (the first letter of actor, signalled by 'originally').
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a dismissive reply expressing indifference, exactly as 'I don't care' does.

clue.text: Conduct was largely good at start of evening

indicators.note: largely means most of the word was, so its final letter is dropped
at start of points to the opening letter of the word evening

explanation.surface: Someone's behaviour was mostly fine as the evening began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' leaves WA from was, then G and the E that opens evening ('at start of').
explanation.definitionFit: To wage a war or campaign is to conduct or carry it on, a verb sense rather than pay.

clue.text: I doubt that oaf is about to show up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
to show means letters inside the run oaf is about are put on display

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts that a clumsy lout is going to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters FISA sit across 'oaF IS About', made visible by 'to show', and 'up' turns them round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The scornful retort expresses disbelief, the colloquial equivalent of saying a claim is unlikely.

clue.text: Close to scene, police in charge encouraging evacuation

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word scene

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Near a crime scene, the officer in command urges people to clear the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evacuation' looks like clearing a building; here it means emptying the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance that induces vomiting, so it promotes emptying of the stomach.

clue.text: Plant hangers designed with petals

indicators.note: designed means arranged to a new pattern, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A gardener's plant holders are made to fit with flower petals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges the thirteen letters of HANGERS and PETALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant grass is a tall African grass species, so it is one example of a plant.

clue.text: Refuse to get secretaries drink

parts.note: PAs are personal assistants, office secretaries
to sup is to drink, sip

explanation.surface: A boss declines to fetch drinks for the office secretaries.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up an opportunity is to decline or turn it down, so the phrasal verb matches refuse.

clue.text: Superior skill keeps Josh's associate at table

indicators.note: keeps means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion
rogan josh is a curry dish, so rogan partners josh on the dinner table

explanation.surface: A clever talent hangs on to Josh's companion at the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: Josh looks like a person; it is half of the curry name rogan josh.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior in the sense of haughty, condescending and looking down on others, as an arrogant person does.

clue.text: Officers not the first choice to convert Poles

parts.note: a sub, or substitute, is used when the first choice is unavailable
to alter is to change or convert
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Second-best officers are told to win Polish people over to a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland; it gives the compass points N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Subalterns are junior army commissioned ranks below captain, so they are military officers.

clue.text: New era shortly — PC state the end of white van man?

indicators.note: new means the letters are formed afresh into a different order
shortly means the word era is cut short, losing its last letter
the end of means the final letter of the word white

explanation.surface: A slogan about political correctness ending the era of the loutish white van driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' shuffles ER ('era shortly'), PC, STATE and E ('the end of white'). White van man is the British stereotype of an aggressive delivery driver; 'van' here is the vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in the van is at the front of a group, which is where a leader setting the speed runs.

clue.text: Queen always surrounded by a lot of old money

indicators.note: surrounded by means the word for always sits inside the other piece
a lot of means most of the word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the guinea was an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A monarch perpetually wrapped up in a large fortune of old coinage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the final A of the coin, and 'surrounded by' wraps it round the word for always.
explanation.definitionFit: Guinevere is King Arthur's wife in legend, a queen of Camelot.

clue.text: Wise old head active in emergencies

indicators.note: active means set in motion, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An experienced sage comes into their own when crises strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'active' rearranges the letters of IN EMERGENCIES.
explanation.definitionFit: An éminence grise is a powerful adviser behind the scenes, a shrewd counsellor wielding influence quietly.

clue.text: Right to live in the city though it did have strings attached

indicators.note: in means the word for live is placed within the other piece

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A right to reside in town, though the deal came with conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strings attached' sounds like conditions on a deal; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebec is a medieval bowed instrument, so it literally had strings fitted.

clue.text: Watch it! He's angling for trouble

definitions.note: a watch is a group, whereas the answer is the plural birds making it up

indicators.note: for trouble means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A warning: a fisherman is looking for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for trouble' shuffles IT and HE'S ANGLING. 'Watch it!' reads as a warning, but 'it' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Watch is the collective noun for a group of these songbirds, an obscure term of venery.

clue.text: Go to collect new guides — they're probably in the office

indicators.note: to collect means the first piece gathers the second inside it

parts.note: go means energy or vigour, which is pep
ushers guide people to their seats

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to fetch new tour guides who are likely at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen-pushers are clerks doing routine paperwork, so they are typically found at a desk.

clue.text: Somewhere in LA likewise being picked up in bar — you can bet on it

indicators.note: in means the sound-alike word goes within the other piece

parts.note: to ban is to bar

indicators.note: being picked up means heard, so a word said aloud is spelt differently

parts.note: too means likewise or also
rouge, red, is a bet on the roulette table

explanation.surface: A gambling tip given in a bar, with a nod to something heard similarly.
explanation.walkthrough: LA is Louisiana, not Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Baton Rouge is the state capital of Louisiana, so it is a place in that state.

clue.text: Hairy bloke in middle of the sauna

indicators.note: in middle of means the letters lie within the run of words the sauna

explanation.surface: A hirsute man sits in the centre of the steam room.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Esau is the twin of Jacob, described as a hairy man.

clue.text: Put in grave situation — people in Northern Territory being detained

parts.note: to inter is to bury, to place in a grave

indicators.note: in means the word for people sits within the abbreviation

parts.note: NT is the abbreviation for Australia's Northern Territory
men means people

explanation.surface: People in Australia's outback find themselves held in custody, a grave state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Internment is confinement without trial, so it is the state of being held prisoner.

clue.text: Crafty old man meets a killer in the house

parts.note: fly is British slang for crafty or knowing
pa is father, informally the old man
per means a, as in once a day

explanation.surface: A cunning old fellow comes face to face with a murderer at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Flypaper is sticky paper hung indoors to trap insects, so it kills them in the home.

clue.text: Debauchery of girl condemned (getting in quick)

indicators.note: getting in means the shuffled letters are placed within the other word

parts.note: pacy means fast or quick

indicators.note: condemned means damned or wrecked, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A girl's wild living is denounced, with a brief aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like an aside, but 'getting in' tells the scrambled letters ('condemned') to enter the word for quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Profligacy is reckless extravagance and dissolute living, close kin to debauchery.

clue.text: When caught only cuddling

indicators.note: cuddling means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: one means only or sole, as in the one person
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A couple caught in nothing more than an embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: As a conjunction, once means as soon as, so it stands for when in a sentence.

clue.text: Risk includes rector touching Norman's neighbour

indicators.note: includes means the first piece holds the second

parts.note: a bet is a risk or gamble
on means touching, as in on the wall

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes a chance by getting physical with the man next door.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman is a person from Normandy, not a name; Brittany adjoins it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Breton comes from Brittany, the French region bordering Normandy.

clue.text: Unseated riders, those unfamiliar with a powerful horse initially restrained

indicators.note: restrained means held in, so the first piece encloses the rest

parts.note: strangers are people unfamiliar to us

indicators.note: initially means the opening letters of the words powerful and horse

explanation.surface: Jockeys thrown off, unused to a strong mount that held them back at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unseated riders' looks like fallen jockeys; it means standing commuters.
explanation.definitionFit: Straphangers are passengers who stand holding straps on a bus or train, travellers with no seat.

clue.text: Clear but doesn't have one idea

indicators.note: doesn't have means a letter is missing from the word

parts.note: plain means clear, obvious
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something obvious, except there's no single concept behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme or proposal, so it serves as a synonym for an idea.

clue.text: Land of the Rising Sun holding American

indicators.note: holding means the first piece keeps the letter for American inside
in a down entry, rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun

explanation.surface: Japan, famed as the land of the rising sun, harbours an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land of the Rising Sun' looks like Japan, but only 'Land' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Laos is a country in Southeast Asia, so it is one example of a nation.

clue.text: Point to Sally's dress

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
a sally is a witty remark, a quip; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A tip pointing towards a woman named Sally's frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a name; it is a witty retort.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress a ship or soldier is to fit out or kit up, the sense of furnishing.

clue.text: Touch wrong handle on boat, some might say

indicators.note: some might say means the words are spoken, and in non-rhotic accents they sound alike

parts.note: sin is wrong and a tiller is the handle steering a boat

explanation.surface: A sailor grabs the wrong handle on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN + TILLER, said in a British accent that drops the final R, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or hint, the sense of a touch of something.

clue.text: Makes dirty joke finally in second bar

indicators.note: in means the final letter goes within the chocolate bar's name

parts.note: Mars is a brand of chocolate bar

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word joke

explanation.surface: A crude gag finally told in a second pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To smear something is to soil it with grease or dirt.

clue.text: Chain fences round square

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: pens are fenced enclosures
nine is a square number, three squared

explanation.surface: Links of a chain fence encircle a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pennines are a range of hills in northern England, a mountain chain.
